summary: Sort is whitelisted, search term is parameterised, and page is clamped, so no injection or unbounded-query problem.

The audit has no result for the payment-verification check even though tests/release/test_payment_verification.py exists, so a critical mandatory check was never recorded. The run was also local only; GO is not supported.

GET /projects trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against user.orgIds, so any logged-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets (IDOR). Validate membership server-side.
RLS is enabled with owner-scoped policies for all operations and anon access is revoked; the update policy's missing WITH CHECK defaults to the USING expression, so owner_id cannot be reassigned.

All mandatory checks pass at the audited commit, and the only finding (no per-account login rate limit, AG-007) is medium with a named owner, approval and compensating edge IP limiting. Release with that accepted risk tracked to its two-week fix.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] sits outside the /api/admin middleware matcher and only calls requireSession, so any authenticated member can permanently delete any user. It needs an admin role check.
The webhook verifies the Stripe signature, requires payment_status paid, handles async success, and records the event id and upgrades the plan in one transaction, so retries are idempotent.

Checkout offers delayed-payment methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance), but the webhook upgrades the plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, granting Pro before payment. The event id is also recorded before processing with a non-atomic check, so a failed update is lost on retry.

The avatar import checks the URL with startsWith on the CDN origin, which accepts https://images.partner-cdn.com.evil.example, and it follows redirects, giving SSRF and arbitrary content. Parse the URL, compare the exact host, disable redirects, and validate the content type and size.
Password reset tokens never expire (AG-004, high, confirmed failing); the team accepted this as a risk but an account-takeover weakness in authentication should be fixed before release, not deferred.
All 25 mandatory checks pass with runtime evidence at the audited commit, there are no findings, and the commit after the audited one only adds the audit file. GO is supported.

The security definer function document_preview has no ownership check, so it bypasses RLS and lets any authenticated user read the title and first 280 characters of any document by id. Make it security invoker or filter on owner_id = auth.uid().

Critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation, payment-verification) are evidenced by no-op commands ('true', 'echo ...') with a fabricated '2 passed' result, so the audit is not credible and the GO is unsupported.

The transfer view does not validate the amount, so a negative amount passes the balance check and moves money from the recipient to the sender. Zero, NaN and a missing recipient also cause errors or 500s; require a finite positive amount with the right precision and handle DoesNotExist.

The critical tenant-isolation check is backed only by static code reading with no runtime test, and src/routes.py actually scopes by owner_id with no organisation filter, so the claim is unverified. Run the runtime test before release.
The invoice route uses findFirst, which is overridden to scope by session userId, so cross-user reads are blocked and a miss returns 404.

The line object spreads client input after name and unitAmount, so a client can override the price (and name) and buy products for any amount. Build lines from server-side product data and take only the validated quantity.
